# Compatibility

<!-- Generated by `cargo run -p branchyard-harness --example compat_matrix > docs/compatibility.md`. Do not edit. -->

Every integration target and driver profile, in the order of the harness registry. Implemented means the driver exists and passes its protocol tests; it does not mean supported. Live qualification ran the profile's driver against the real harness binary as a local process, not inside a Branchyard sandbox, so isolation, credentials and recovery remain unqualified for every profile. See [driver qualification](qualification/README.md) for scope and findings, and [writing a driver](writing-a-driver.md) to add a row.

Capabilities are what the driver offers before negotiation. ACP resume is used only when the agent advertises `session/resume` or `session/load`; a session that cannot resume fails to open rather than starting fresh. "Checked against" names the harness version whose transcript or generated schema the driver's frames were compared with. "Reasons" names why each `no` capability (and any `yes`/`if advertised` with a real caveat) is that way, quoted from the driver's own refusal message or documentation; `not verified` marks a gap with no such evidence yet, never a guess.

"Perm. answered" and "Steer" are the two gates Branchyard can intercept mid-turn: a tool permission request it answers, and input it delivers into a running turn without ending it. Each is `—` when the driver does not offer it at all (nothing to intercept); otherwise `live-tested` (checked against a real installed binary — a qualification report's Policy area for permissions, or `docs/harness-integration.md` "Steering a running turn"'s recorded evidence for steer), `contract-only` (only the conformance kit's own mocked protocol test, run for every profile regardless of qualification), or `not verified` (offered, but neither) — never overstated.\n
"Budget" is whether the harness enforces a spending limit itself: Branchyard gives such a harness what is left of the branch's `max_usd` for each turn, so it stops before it goes over; for every harness, Branchyard still stops a turn once the cost the harness reports crosses the limit ([budgets](delegation.md#budgets)).

## Install, sign-in and key

What `by harnesses --all` lists for each harness above, from the [harness catalog](../catalog/harnesses.toml): the executables to look for, the recommended install command, the command that signs in through the CLI itself, and the variables that carry an API key instead. Whether a machine has each, and whether it is logged in, is that machine's inventory ([harness lifecycle](harness-lifecycle.md#how-detection-works)).

| Harness | Executables | Install | Sign in | API key variables |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| Claude Code (`claude-code`) | `claude` | `curl -fsSL https://claude.ai/install.sh \| bash` | `claude auth login` | `ANTHROPIC_API_KEY` |
| Codex (`codex`) | `codex` | `npm install -g @openai/codex` | `codex login --device-auth` | `OPENAI_API_KEY` |
| Antigravity (`antigravity`) | `agy`, `antigravity` | `curl -fsSL https://antigravity.google/cli/install.sh \| bash` | `agy` | `GEMINI_API_KEY` |
| Oh My Pi (`oh-my-pi`) | `omp` | `curl -fsSL https://omp.sh/install \| sh` | `omp login` | `GEMINI_API_KEY`, `OPENAI_API_KEY`, `ANTHROPIC_API_KEY`, `OPENROUTER_API_KEY`, `ZAI_API_KEY` |
| DeepSeek Harness (`deepseek-harness`) | `dsh` | `npm install -g @deepseek-ai/dsh` | — | `DEEPSEEK_API_KEY` |
| Gemini CLI (`gemini-cli`) | `gemini` | `npm install -g @google/gemini-cli` | `gemini` | `GEMINI_API_KEY`, `GOOGLE_API_KEY` |
| OpenCode (`opencode`) | `opencode`, `opencode2` | `npm install -g opencode-ai` | `opencode auth login` | `ANTHROPIC_API_KEY`, `OPENAI_API_KEY`, `GEMINI_API_KEY`, `ORCAROUTER_API_KEY` |
| Pi (`pi`) | `pi` | `npm install -g @earendil-works/pi-coding-agent --ignore-scripts` | — | — |
| Goose (`goose`) | `goose` | `curl -fsSL https://github.com/aaif-goose/goose/releases/download/stable/download_cli.sh \| bash` | — | — |
| Cursor CLI (`cursor`) | `cursor-agent` | `curl https://cursor.com/install -fsS \| bash` | — | — |
| GitHub Copilot CLI (`github-copilot`) | `copilot` | `npm install -g @github/copilot` | — | — |
| Amp (`amp`) | `amp` | `npm install -g @ampcode/cli` | — | — |
| Qwen Code (`qwen-code`) | `qwen` | `npm install -g @qwen-code/qwen-code` | — | — |
| Kimi CLI (`kimi-cli`) | `kimi`, `kimi-code` | `curl -LsSf https://code.kimi.com/install.sh \| bash` | — | — |
| Hermes (`hermes`) | `hermes` | `curl -fsSL https://hermes-agent.nousresearch.com/install.sh \| bash` | — | — |

Checked by running the CLIs (Codex 0.157.1, Antigravity CLI 1.3.3, Gemini CLI 0.63.0, DeepSeek Harness 0.2.0-rc.2, Oh My Pi 18.10.3):

- **Codex** signs in headless with `codex login --device-auth`; `codex login status` prints `Logged in using ChatGPT`, and the login is the file `~/.codex/auth.json` (Branchyard's provisioner takes it as the `CODEX_AUTH` secret). `CODEX_API_KEY` or `OPENAI_API_KEY` is the key.
- **Antigravity** reads a key from `GEMINI_API_KEY` alone (`GOOGLE_API_KEY` has no effect), and only when `~/.gemini/antigravity-cli/settings.json` has `"modelProvider": "gemini"`; otherwise it asks for a Google sign-in, which a headless run cannot give. Branchyard sets the setting in isolated runs; `by harnesses` says when it is missing.
- **Gemini CLI** takes `GEMINI_API_KEY`. Its headless `gemini -p` refuses an untrusted directory unless `GEMINI_CLI_TRUST_WORKSPACE=true` (or `--skip-trust`).
- **DeepSeek Harness** is the `dsh` binary (not `dsh-tui` or `dst`, which only launch its terminal profile). It has no sign-in command: `DEEPSEEK_API_KEY` feeds its shipped provider (`deepseek-official`), and a provider in `$DSH_HOME/cordis.patch.yml` (default `~/.dsh`) or in `profiles/acp/cordis.patch.yml` replaces it; `dsh --profile acp --dump-config` prints the composed configuration.
- **Oh My Pi** (`omp`) is a Bun script that needs Bun 1.3.14 or newer on `PATH`: under an older Bun it fails to parse and `omp --version` exits 1 (`by harnesses` says so), and its installer installs or upgrades Bun where `npm install -g` or `bun install -g` of `@oh-my-pi/pi-coding-agent` does not. A provider key in the environment (`GEMINI_API_KEY`, `OPENAI_API_KEY`, `ANTHROPIC_API_KEY`, `OPENROUTER_API_KEY`, or `ZAI_API_KEY` for its `zai` provider, GLM) is enough: with the Gemini key alone it ran on `gemini-3.1-pro-preview`, its default for that provider, and `modelRoles.default` in `~/.omp/agent/config.yml` picks another, which Branchyard's provisioner writes from `--model`. `omp login PROVIDER` stores an OAuth login in `~/.omp/agent/agent.db`, which `by harnesses` reads for provider names when the machine has `sqlite3` or `python3`. Over ACP it asks before commands, deletions and moves and not before writes, so a `read-only` policy is also written into its config as per-tool `deny` policies ([provisioning](provisioning.md#oh-my-pi-tool-policies)).

## Known, not driven

The harness registry names 48 CLIs. Beside the rows above, Branchyard knows these 33 from the vendored Herdr, Scion, emdash, Orca, agentapi and Coder Registry sources, with no profile to drive them: `aider`, `cline`, `devin`, `droid`, `grok-build`, `kilo`, `kiro`, `letta`, `maki`, `mastracode`, `muse-code`, `qodercli`, `ante`, `auggie`, `autohand`, `codebuddy`, `codebuff`, `command-code`, `continue`, `crush`, `freebuff`, `jules`, `junie`, `mimo-code`, `mistral-vibe`, `openclaude`, `openclaw`, `prime-agent`, `rovo-dev`, `trae`, `zcode`, `zero`, `amazon-q`. `by harnesses --all` lists every one with its install and login commands, API-key variables and models where upstream records them ([`catalog/harnesses.toml`](../catalog/harnesses.toml), generated from the pinned sources); knowing a CLI is not support for it.

## On your machines

This page says what Branchyard can drive. Whether a machine can run a harness is that machine's inventory: `by harnesses` shows which are installed there, at which version, whether each is logged in and how much of its quota is used; `by harnesses install`, `update` and `login` act on one under `[harnesses]` policy; workers advertise theirs, and the router uses it. See [harness lifecycle](harness-lifecycle.md).
